Proven experience designing, deploying, and operating large-scale (petabyte-class) high-performance parallel and distributed file systems (e.g., Lustre, Ceph, BeeGFS, GPFS), as well as enterprise and local file systems (e.g., NFS, ZFS, ext4, XFS) in Linux-based environments, including troubleshooting and performance tuning.
Expert knowledge and experience with large data storage arrays (more than100TB), and methods to administer, monitor and upgrade.

Proven experience administering and supporting large-scale HPC clusters or other distributed POSIX (Linux) systems, including advanced knowledge of Linux system administration, primarily Red Hat and its derivatives (e.g., Rocky Linux).

The Sr. High-Performance Computing (HPC) Engineer will be responsible for the technical operation of AWARE, CW3E’s high-performance computing system. Working with the CW3E Research Cyberinfrastructure Lead, this person will take the lead on system administration, maintenance, upgrades, deployments, and troubleshooting. AWARE supports both time-sensitive "near realtime" operational forecasting and research, so system availability and careful planning of changes are important parts of the job.

The work covers the full HPC environment, including compute and GPU nodes, Ethernet and InfiniBand networks, parallel storage, cluster management, job scheduling, authentication, monitoring, and data-transfer services. The engineer will install and integrate new hardware and software, maintain system configurations and automation, monitor performance and capacity, and respond to production problems. They will also coordinate with campus teams and vendors when outside support is needed and maintain documentation for system changes, procedures, and recovery.

A significant part of the job involves working directly with researchers and operational workflow managers. The engineer will help troubleshoot jobs, MPI applications, software environments, containers, memory and I/O problems, and CPU/GPU performance. This requires being able to determine whether an issue is coming from the application, software environment, scheduler, network, storage system, or hardware and then work with the appropriate people to resolve it.

The engineer will help the CW3E Research Cyberinfrastructure Lead plan future additions and upgrades to AWARE. This may include gathering requirements, comparing technical options, developing benchmarks, working through procurements, and planning deployments with as little disruption as possible.

As a senior member of the group, the engineer will also be expected to share knowledge with other staff. This includes mentoring team members, explaining HPC concepts, reviewing technical work, and improving the documentation needed to operate and support the system.

The position requires applicable experience supporting HPC, research computing, or large-scale Linux systems. Experience with technologies used at CW3E, such as Slurm, InfiniBand, BeeGFS or Lustre, ZFS, MPI, GPU computing, configuration-management platforms (BCM, xcat), and system-monitoring & metric tools (telegraf, influxdb, nagios), is desired but not required. Experience with comparable systems and the ability to learn and troubleshoot unfamiliar technologies will also be considered.
Advanced knowledge of systems integration deploying complex systems integration solutions.
Advanced skills associated with system integration design, modification, implementation and deployment in a complex environment.
Demonstrated ability to develop complex conversion and system implementation plans.
Demonstrated ability to understand functional needs of the campus / medical center and / or UC system and how systems can support those needs.
Demonstrated ability to interface with senior level technical and non-technical management on a regular basis.
Demonstrated ability to create software specifications.
Ability to impart knowledge to senior level technical and non-technical audiences and to influence outcomes to meet objectives.
Demonstrated ability to identify software and hardware interdependences in a complex multi-platform environment.
Demonstrated ability to develop solutions for complex business and systems / custom / ad-hoc solutions.
Demonstrated ability to plan and execute the technical aspects of deploying, upgrading, and decommissioning storage systems.
Demonstrated knowledge of TCP/IP and Infiniband networking, including sockets, VLANs, and firewalls.
Advanced knowledge of HPC middleware stack including cluster management tools, job schedulers and resources managers. Examples include: Slurm, PBS, HPCM, and Bright Cluster Manager.
